segments.text: Good afternoon, this is Aakashwani and I am Saira Muchthaba with the Mid-Day News.
The Headlines
Very severe cyclonic storm or nub completes its landfall along Andhra Pradesh coast.
Heavy rain lashes several parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh, Orissa and Yannam.
Several flights and train services affected.
Severe cyclonic storm likely to weaken into cyclonic storm during the next three hours.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his US counterpart Pete Hexeth review progress of 10-year India-US
defence framework. Prime Minister Binyamin Netanyahu liquid block leads on 57 out of 120
seats in early results of parliamentary Israeli election. And in women's cricket, Zimbabwe
win toss and elect to bat first against India in 3rd ODI at Vadodara.
And now the news in detail.
Very severe cyclonic storm or NERB has completed its landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
The Intermetrological Department said, the storm crossed the coast between Bapatla and
Vishakhapatnam near Narsapur and southwest of Yhanam earlier this morning.
At the time of landfall, the cyclone brought maximum sustained winds of 125 to 135 km
kilometers per hour, with gusts reaching 150 kilometers per hour.
The landfall process was completed by 8 a.m., with the storm's central region moving entirely
over land.
The system is likely to move north-northwestwards and gradually weaken into a cyclonic storm
within the next three hours and further into a deep depression during the following six
hours.
Meanwhile, Andhra Desh, Chief Minister in Chandrababu, Naitu, has written to Union
home minister mature, seeking early deployment of central teams to assess the damage caused
by Cyclone Ornab in the state. In his letter, the chief minister said the Cyclone had damaged
crops, houses, roads and electricity infrastructure. He said 16 NTRF and 11 STRF teams had been
deployed across 14 districts, while more than 28,000 people had been shifted to rehabilitation
centres. No loss of life has been reported so far.
The state government has issued emergency helpline numbers 1070 and 112.
Mr. Knight also sought continued support from central agencies for relief and rehabilitation.
The authorities have evacuated over 1,80,000 people to safer zones and relief shelters
across the states of Andhra Pradesh and Orissa.
More than 100 train services have been cancelled or rescheduled.
Let's go live to our Anth Pradesh correspondent for more updates.
What is the current situation on the ground after the landfall of the cyclone?
Hello, Sairan.
Cyclone has not completed its landfall along the Anth Pradesh coast this morning and we
can introduce severe cyclonic storm.
Heavy rainfall and storm winds have affected several coastal districts, particularly Kona
Seema, Kakinada, East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna and Anacapalli.
According to the state government's preliminary assessment, no loss of human life has been
reported so far.
Around 180 houses have been damaged and more than 220 trees have fallen on roads.
Our supply has been disrupted in sub-ghostal areas, while crops in several areas have
been inundated.
The administration is prioritizing roads clearance, restoration of electricity and
drinking water supply and release for affected families.
Right. Thank you. What are the steps that is the, you know, the authorities taking to carry out relief and rescue operations?
The government has deployed 16 NDRF teams and 11 SDRF teams across 14 districts. More than 28,000 people have been shifted to relief sector as a precautionary measure.
District collectors are coordinating rescue and relief operations supported by emergency
control rooms functioning around the clock.
Medical teams, ambulances and essential relief supplies have been positioned in affected
areas.
High services personnel have attended to more than 220 emergency calls, mostly involving
the removal of fallen trees.
Road clearance and electricity restoration teams are working to restore essential
services.

The government has directed officials to ensure drinking water, food, and medical assistance for affected families, and to continue relief operations until the threat from heavy rain and strong floods subsides.
Chief Minister and Chandra Babu Naidu has written to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, seeking the early deployment of central teams to assess the damage caused by cyclone earn-up in the state.
Right. Thanks a lot, Murali, for that update.
In Orissa, the Intermetrological Department has forecast heavy to extremely heavy rainfall,
strong winds and possible flash floods in several southern districts.
Train services have been disrupted, while bus connectivity between Bhuvaneswar and southern
Orissa has also phased precautionary restrictions.
The next 24 hours remain crucial for flood monitoring, public safety and restoration
of essential services across the affected districts.
Let's hear more from our correspondent.
In Odisha, the immediate concern is the possibility of flash floods and water logging following
intense rainfall associated with Cyclone Arnab.
As the Cyclone completed its landfall near Yanam this morning and weakened into a severe
cyclone storm, the IMD said it will weaken further into a deep depression by this evening
and cross Malkangiri in Odisha.
Ganjam, Gajapati, Raigada, Kuraput and Malkangiri are among the districts facing significant
rainfall and flash flood risks.
Navrangpur is also experiencing heavy rainfall.
IMD has warned of strong winds with gusts potentially reaching 80 kilometers per hour in southern
districts.
Some northern districts will also have heavy rain with strong winds.
The sea remains dangerous, and fishermen have been advised not to venture out.
Railway services have been cancelled or regulated as a precaution, while bus services to southern
Odisha have faced disruption.
The state government has kept rescue teams ready, arranged shelters and directed
officials to protect vulnerable residents and restore essential services, the next 24
hours are critical for Odisha, even as the cyclone weekends, accumulated rainfall, swell
and streams, and sudden flooding may pose serious risks.
Prakash Das, Forakaswani News, Bhuvaneswar
The cyclone has caused widespread damages in the Yanam region of Puducherry.
Standing crops in baddie fields were inundated.
Fishermen lost large stalks of dried fish stored in fish-drying platforms on coast.
more details from our correspondent.
During landfall in Yenam, strong winds blew at speeds ranging from 125 to 135 km per hour,
occasionally reaching 150 km per hour.
Trees and electricity poles were uprooted at several places, blocking roads and disrupting power supply.
In Savitri Nagar and other coastal villages, flood water entered several houses
and affected people were accommodated in schools and cyclone shelters.
In Yenam, 300 personnel from the Puducherry Police, the India Reserve Battalion and the
National Disaster Response Force are continuing relief and rescue operations.
Srinivasan RNU Puducherry with the inputs from Sivashesh Babu at Yenam.
Inspector General of National Disaster Response Force NDRF Narendra Singh Bundela today said
that Northern Andhra Pradesh and Southern Odisha have been burst affected by its cyclone
or NERB.
briefing media in New Delhi, Mr. Bundela said that NDRF and SDRF teams are currently deployed
in the affected areas in coordination with the state and central governments.
The cyclone has completely entered the landmass.
Based on wind speed, it has been downgraded from a very severe cyclonic storm to a severe
cyclonic storm.
It is expected to weaken further into a cyclonic storm within the next six hours
by around noon and subsequently downgrade into a deep depression by the evening.
Northern Andhra Pradesh and Southern Udisha have been the worst affected regions so far.
Besides strong winds, several districts have also received significant rainfall.
The affected districts in Andhra Pradesh include Visakhapatnam, Vijayanagaraam, Anakapalli
and Srikakulam.
In Southern Udisha, Koraput, Ganjam and Gajapati have also received significant
rainfall.
In the wake of cyclonic storm Urnab, the Civil Aviation Ministry has reviewed the situation
and taken measures to ensure aviation safety.
The ministry noted that flights to and from coastal Andhra Desh and southern Orissa are
expected to be most affected.
Hyderabad, Varanasi, Prayagraj and Gorakhpur may also witness knock-on delays depending
on the storm's track.
back.
Unit Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Pratap Rao Jadhav today launched the
fourth edition of the Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign 4.0 in New Delhi. The campaign marks a significant
advancement in India's tobacco control efforts, focusing on preventing tobacco initiation
among young people and supporting individuals who wish to quit. Speaking on the occasion,
Mr. Jadhav stated that the primary objective of the campaign is to keep young people
away from tobacco use, enabling them to contribute to the nation's development.
Punjab-Vidhan Sabha has urged the Centre to facilitate the reopening of the Shri
Kartarpur Sahib Corridor and ensure regular, hassle-free access for the Sikh
Sangat to pay obeisance at Gurudwara Shri Darbar Sahib. Passing a resolution on the last day
of the session yesterday, it demanded that the union government may take immediate steps
to reopen the corridor and keep it operational. This is Akash Varni giving you the news.
Welcome back, you are listening to Midday News. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today
held a meeting with US Secretary of War Pete Hexeth on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN
Defense Minister's meeting, ADMM+, in Philippines. In a social media post, Mr Singh said that
they had reviewed the progress of 10-year inter-US defense framework, driving strategic
convergence across military technology, information sharing and co-production. He said that robust
partnership of both the nations continues to be a cornerstone for a free, open and
secure Indo-Pacific.
India and Mexico have taken a significant step towards strengthening their economic
partnership, with the signing of the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement.
The signing formally marks the launch of negotiations for a mutually beneficial and balanced agreement
aimed at expanding bilateral trade, creating new business opportunities, boosting investment
flows and building resilient and diversified supply chains. The Terms of Reference were
signed by Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal and Mexico's Undersecretary of Foreign
trade, Luis Rojento-Guitarres Romano in Mexico. The framework outlines key areas for negotiation,
including market access for goods, rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation,
dispute settlement and technical barriers to trade.
In Israel, election results showed incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's liquid block,
leading when reports last came in, with 41.9% of the ballot boxes countered.
The partial results released by the Central Elections Committee gave Netanyahu's block
57 seeds to 47 for the anti-Netanyahu camp.
The predominantly Arab joint list and ram factions together held the remaining 16 seeds.
India aims to develop 5 million metric tons of annual green hydrogen production capacity
The government has said that this transition can reduce dependence on imported fossil
fossil fuels, and strengthen the country's long-term energy security.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission marks an important step towards building a cleaner,
more self-reliant and globally competitive energy economy.
The mission is expected to reduce cumulative fossil fuel imports by approximately 1 lakh
crore rupees by 2030.
The mission seeks to create new opportunities for industrial growth, investment and employment.
It is expected to mobilize over 8 lakh crore rupees in investments and generate more
than six lakh jobs across manufacturing, infrastructure, research and project development.
Union Education Minister Prehla Joshi today attended the inaugural session of the Clean
Sports Conclave along with Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr. Mansukh
Montoya. During the event, a Memorandum of Understanding for Sport Values in Every
Classroom, or SWEVET, was assigned among the Education, Youth Affairs Ministry and
UNESCO. In a social media post, Mr. Joshi said that the agreement marks a significant
can step towards embedding sporting values in school education in alignment with the
vision of national education policy 2020.
In women's cricket, Zimbabwe were 12 for 1 in 2.1 overs against India in the third and
final ODI match in Vadodara, when reports last came in. Earlier, Zimbabwe won the
toss and elected to bat first.
The union government has taken serious note of the death of a 19-month-old male
Chita, KNG 2-2, at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh due to firearm pellet injuries.
The centre has deputed a high-level team to conduct an on-ground investigation into the
incident, given the critical importance of Project Chita.
The Chita was found injured on 25th October in the territorial forest of Morena, outside
the protected area of Kuno National Park.
And now before we enter bulletin the headlines once again.
Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab completes its landfall along Ant Pradesh coast.
Heavy rain lashes several parts of coastal Ant Pradesh, southern Odisha and Yanam.
Several flights and train services affected.
Severe cyclonic storm likely to weaken into cyclonic storm during the next three hours.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his US counterpart Pete Hexeth review progress
of 10-year India-US Defence Framework.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's liquids block leads in 57 out of 120 seats in early
results of Israeli parliamentary elections, and in women's cricket, Zimbabwe win toss
and elect to bat first against India in 3rd ODI at Vadodra.
And with that, we end the midday news.
